title: 消费与劳动阅读词汇
goal: 辨认消费与劳动词汇，理解经济变化对不同群体的影响。

points.label: 辨认消费与劳动领域词汇
理解经济变化对不同群体的影响

sources.title: 全国大学英语四、六级考试大纲
sources.used: 阅读课程内容与材料形式

body.p: 消费与劳动类文章常讨论价格、需求、工作机会和劳动保障。同一个变化，对消费者、经营者和劳动者的影响往往不同。

body.box: A shop offers home delivery. Customers save a journey, while staff spend more time preparing orders.

body.p: 顾客少跑一趟，员工多了准备订单的工作。评价一个变化，要分开看每个群体受到什么影响。

body.box:
A neighborhood grocery began accepting orders for collection in the evening. Customers could select goods earlier in the day and collect them after work. Some customers valued the shorter time spent inside the shop. Others continued to choose goods in person, especially produce they preferred to examine themselves.

The new service also changed how employees worked. Staff prepared orders during quieter hours, but the evening collection period required someone to remain at the counter later. The owner added paid hours for two employees who wanted them. Other employees preferred their existing schedules and did not take the extra shifts. The change created additional paid work for some people without affecting everyone in the same way.

The owner compared revenue from orders with the cost of staff time and packaging. An increase in orders did not by itself show whether the service covered its costs. The decision to continue depended on both customer demand and the resources needed to provide the service.

body.p: 第一段比较两类顾客的选择：部分顾客节省店内时间，另一些顾客仍偏好亲自挑选。
第二段区分员工对班次的不同偏好。第三段的 revenue 指收入，cost 指成本。订单增加了，还要和成本一起看。

groups.fill: A bakery introduced an afternoon collection service. The ser{vice} lets cust{omers} order br{ead} in adv{ance} and col{lect} their purc{hases} after wo{rk}. The bak{ery} records ord{ers} and st{aff} wages separately. Some customers prefer collecting on their way home, while others still buy bread in the morning. Employees spend time preparing the orders before collection. The owner compares the income from the service with the costs of labor and packaging. Those figures help the bakery assess whether the service can continue.
notes: collect：后文 collection 复现取货行为。
staff：staff wages 表示员工工资。

groups.text:
A clothing shop began offering repairs for garments purchased there. Customers could pay to replace a zip or mend a seam instead of buying a replacement garment immediately. Some valued being able to continue wearing a familiar item. Others preferred to buy new clothing rather than wait for a repair. The service therefore attracted only part of the shop's customer base.

The shop trained two employees to assess items and arrange repairs with a local tailor. These employees gained additional responsibilities, while the tailor received work from the shop. The shop also had to spend staff time recording orders and answering questions. It compared the fees collected with those costs before deciding whether to extend the service.

A higher number of repair orders did not necessarily mean higher overall profit. Materials, staff time and payments to the tailor also mattered. The owner gathered information about customers' waiting times and the condition of returned garments. The assessment considered the experience of customers and workers as well as the financial result.

items.stem: Why did some customers value the repair service?
options: It let them keep using familiar clothing.
It made every repair free of charge.
It let them buy new clothes without waiting.
It cost less than buying a new garment.
items.why: 原文说 Some valued being able to continue wearing a familiar item，第一项是它的改写。第三项是另一部分顾客的想法。

items.stem: What new responsibility did the trained employees take on?
options: Mending garments for the local tailor
Assessing items and arranging repairs
Training other staff to mend seams
Recording the tailor's waiting times
items.why: trained two employees to assess items and arrange repairs 指出新增职责。

items.stem: Why did the owner compare fees with costs?
options: To set the fee for replacing a zip
To avoid collecting information about waiting times
To judge whether to offer repairs more widely
To decide whether to train more employees
items.why: 原文说 compared the fees collected with those costs before deciding whether to extend the service。第三项把 extend the service 改写为 offer repairs more widely。

items.stem: What does garments mean in the first paragraph?
options: Repair fees the shop paid to a tailor
Orders recorded by employees
Materials the tailor used to mend seams
Items of clothing bought at the shop
items.why: garments 可继续穿着并可更换拉链，指衣物。

items.stem: Which expense is included in the assessment?
options: Fees the shop paid to the local tailor
Customers' earlier clothing purchases
Fees collected for completed repairs
The price of new replacement garments
items.why: 原文把 payments to the tailor 列为要考虑的成本，即第一项。第三项是收入，不是支出。

groups.fill: A furniture shop rents tables for short events. The sh{op} checks ea{ch} table bef{ore} delivery a{nd} records i{ts} condition wh{en} it ret{urns}. Staff th{en} clean t{he} tables bef{ore} the next rental. Customers can use a table without buying one, while the shop must store and maintain its stock. The owner compares rental income with transport and repair costs. This comparison helps establish whether the service is financially workable. Customer demand may also vary between seasons.

groups.text:
A neighborhood bicycle shop began renting bicycles for short journeys. Customers who needed a bicycle occasionally could rent one without paying the full purchase price. Some customers valued the lower initial expense, while others preferred owning a bicycle that was always available. The rental service was an additional choice rather than a replacement for sales.

The shop hired a mechanic for extra hours to inspect returned bicycles. The mechanic welcomed the additional paid work, but the owner had to include wages and replacement parts in the cost of the service. During busy periods, customers could reserve bicycles in advance. The shop also needed space to store them between rentals.

After several months, the owner compared rental income with the cost of inspection, repairs and storage. A large number of rentals did not automatically establish that the service was profitable. The owner also asked customers whether bicycles were available when needed. The decision to continue would depend on financial results and service quality as well as demand. These measures captured different aspects of the service and were considered together.

items.stem: What did some customers value about renting?
options: It guaranteed ownership of a bicycle.
It required a smaller initial payment than buying.
It removed the need to reserve during busy periods.
It eliminated all charges for repairs and storage.
items.why: lower initial expense 说明租用的初始支出较低。

items.stem: How did the service affect the mechanic?
options: It ended the need to inspect bicycles.
It removed the shop's need for replacement parts.
It provided additional paid inspection work.
It reduced the mechanic's regular hours.
items.why: hired a mechanic for extra hours to inspect returned bicycles 表明增加了有偿工作。

items.stem: What does reserve mean in the second paragraph?
options: Arrange in advance to use a bicycle
Repair a bicycle after it is returned
Buy a bicycle at the full price
Store replacement parts between rentals
items.why: reserve bicycles in advance 表示提前预留自行车。

items.stem: Why did the owner examine costs as well as income?
options: To count how many rentals were made
To avoid checking whether bicycles were available
To set the mechanic's hourly wages
To judge whether renting made a profit
items.why: 原文说 A large number of rentals did not automatically establish that the service was profitable，所以要把收入和成本放在一起看，即第四项。第一项只看租用次数。

items.stem: What does demand refer to in the final paragraph?
options: The wages paid for bicycle inspection
Customers' interest in renting bicycles
The parts needed to repair returned bicycles
The space used to store rental bicycles
items.why: demand 与租赁次数和顾客是否需要自行车有关，指租赁需求。
